claim_summary: Trains tool-using vision-language weather agents with a two-stage RL curriculum (verifiable questions, then forecast-discussion reports) and a grounding-gated rubric and claim-entailment report reward, in an environment with plotting observations.

claim_evidence.quote: We develop Zephyrus-R1 (Figure 1), an agentic framework for weather-report generation in which a vision-language model acquires evidence through tools, synthesizes information across regions and lead times, and optimizes an openended report-level objective.

modules.name: Verifiable-question to report curriculum RL
modules.scope_reason: R2 gives LLM: LoRA rejection-sampling fine-tuning and CISPO RL update policy parameters in both stages. The verifier and the grounded reward are Harness modules and are listed separately.

therefore use a two-stage curriculum: Stage 1 trains tool use on verifiable weather-analysis questions; Stage 2 optimizes

Both RL stages use CISPO with group-centered advantages, 16 prompts and four rollouts per step, temperature 0.6, zero KL regularization, and rank-64 LoRA on the language layers with the vision tower frozen

modules.name: Grounding-gated rubric and claim-entailment report reward
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 holds: the rubric and claim-level F1 embed the forecast-discussion requirement, and the grounding gate requires dataset access and forecast fields at a lead before a report is accepted. A different report task needs a redesigned reward and gate.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - rubric, claim F1 and the grounding gate embed the forecast-discussion requirement; counterfactual: all change for another report task

evidence.quote: Report Grounding Requirement. To ensure that the model actually examines the atmospheric data rather than hallucinating a plausible report, we require a minimum amount of successful tool use before assigning a judge-based reward.
Rubric Score. We first construct a meteorological rubric that captures the qualities of a strong forecast discussion.
Discussion F1. We also measure factual agreement at the level of individual claims.
The grounding state is maintained by the execution server and reset at the start of every episode. It contains three cumulative Boolean conditions.

modules.name: Graded verifier with required-tool check for verifiable questions
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK: yes, the score ladder over numerical, location, time and anomaly answers and the required-tool condition are tied to these question types; another question family needs a different verifier. It checks answers and tool access, not temporal evidence, so no temporal function is claimed.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - answer-type score ladder and required-tool check

evidence.quote: The verifier gives graded credit for numerical, location, time, and anomaly answers.
The required-tool condition holds when the server records at least one call to the dataset or climatology tool, whichever the question requires.

modules.name: Plotting tool returning image observations
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK: no, plotting embeds no report objective. R3_2_GTS: no, it plots arbitrary images without assuming temporal order, window or availability. R3_3_GH: yes, it extends the tool interface and observation channel.

evidence.quote: In this work, we augment the environment by adding vision capabilities to the agent. It can now leverage a plotting tool to plot arbitrary images during its code interactions.
